name: Otto Heinrich Warburg
summary: German biochemist and physiologist known for discovering the Warburg effect and identifying the respiratory ferment.

name: Emil Warburg
summary: German physicist and father of Otto Warburg.

name: Emil Fischer
summary: German chemist and Nobel laureate who mentored Otto Warburg.

name: Otto Meyerhof
summary: German physician and biochemist who collaborated with Warburg.

name: Hans Krebs
summary: German-born British biochemist who worked in Warburg's lab.

name: University of Freiburg
summary: German university where Warburg studied chemistry.

name: University of Berlin
summary: German university where Warburg studied under Emil Fischer.

name: University of Heidelberg
summary: German university where Warburg studied medicine.

name: Kaiser Wilhelm Institute
summary: German research institute where Warburg worked as a principal investigator.

name: Institute of Cell Physiology
summary: Berlin institute founded for Warburg with Rockefeller funding.

name: Max Planck Institute
summary: Institute converted from Warburg's Institute of Cell Physiology in 1952.

name: Rockefeller Foundation
summary: American foundation that funded Warburg's institute.

name: Nobel Prize
summary: Prestigious award received by Warburg in 1931.

name: Warburg effect
summary: Metabolic phenotype of tumor cells characterized by high aerobic glycolysis.

name: Freiburg in Breisgau
summary: German city where Otto Warburg was born.

name: Berlin
summary: German city where Warburg lived and worked for most of his career.
